newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade slow, steady - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade slow, steady - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales near midday Friday were very slow at a top of $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from the bulk of this week's trade, feedlot sources said. There were a few sales this week at $64.25.
About 200 head of slaughter steers and heifers likely to grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area Friday following weekly sales near 93,400 there, sources said.

The Panhandle showlist was estimated near 81,500 head earlier in the week. There were no reported sales in Kansas Friday morning following weekly sales near 90,800 head. The showlist in Kansas had been pegged near 92,500.

The $64.00 price this week was up $1.00 from last week, with gains attributed to a steep advance in wholesale beef prices. Beef values soared on tight packer stocks and demand from retailers booking orders for Independence Day holiday advertising features, market sources said.
By Thursday, choice beef weighing 700/850 lbs was quoted at $103.79 per cwt, up $5.67 since last Friday, USDA said.
However, beef prices at midday Friday were quoted down $0.10 to $0.37. Heavyweight choice was quoted at $103.42, down $0.37 from Thursday, USDA statistics showed.
